name: Incident Response Lifecycle (4 Stages)
command: # IR Lifecycle: Preparation → Detection & Analysis → Containment/Eradication/Recovery → Post-Incident Activity
description: The four-stage incident handling process as defined by NIST SP 800-61. Each stage has clear objectives and feeds the next.
notes:
Stage 1 — Preparation: Build the capability to respond. Policies, playbooks, communication plans, jump bags, training, TheHive/SIEM setup.
Stage 2 — Detection & Analysis: Identify and validate incidents. Alert triage, log correlation, IOC extraction, severity classification, stakeholder notification.
Stage 3 — Containment/Eradication/Recovery: Limit damage (isolate hosts, block IPs, disable accounts), remove root cause (delete malware, patch), restore operations.
Stage 4 — Post-Incident Activity: Lessons learned meeting, root cause analysis, update playbooks, report to management, close case in TheHive.

examples.label: Stage 1 — Preparation checklist
examples.command: # Verify: playbooks current, TheHive accessible, SIEM ingesting, jump bag stocked, contacts list updated

examples.label: Stage 2 — Initial triage questions
examples.command: # What triggered? When first seen? What assets affected? Any data accessed/exfiltrated? Severity?

examples.label: Stage 3 — Immediate containment steps
examples.command: # Isolate host → block C2 at firewall → disable compromised account → preserve forensic image

examples.label: Stage 4 — Post-incident checklist
examples.command: # Schedule lessons-learned meeting → document timeline → update detection rules → close TheHive case

references.title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev 2 - Computer Security Incident Handling Guide

recommended.note: TheHive for case management throughout the IR lifecycle.
Classify the incident type during Detection & Analysis.
